query: For a titanium- and nickel-containing high-entropy alloy in a single-phase solid-solution state, whose elevated-temperature mechanical performance remains unestablished when titanium and nickel serve as primary constituents rather than additions, what single testable intervention hypothesis could produce better mechanical properties under elevated-temperature or extreme-environment testing than the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, mechanism, predicted relative outcome, applicable composition and test-regime boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Thermomechanical treatment of the Ti-Ni high-entropy alloy will improve its mechanical properties, such as yield strength and ultimate tensile strength, under elevated-temperature and extreme-environment testing conditions.
generation.intervention: Thermomechanical treatment (e.g., hot rolling, cold rolling, and rapid annealing)
generation.conditions: Elevated-temperature testing (e.g., 600°C) and extreme-environment testing (e.g., corrosion resistance in 0.5 M H2SO4 solution)
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a single body-centered cubic structure with improved grain refinement and reduced defects
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement and defect reduction due to thermomechanical treatment
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties (e.g., yield strength, ultimate tensile strength) and corrosion resistance compared to the baseline Ti-Ni high-entropy alloy without thermomechanical treatment
generation.baseline: Ti-Ni high-entropy alloy without thermomechanical treatment
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the thermomechanical treatment parameters and the potential for over-reliance on specific treatment parameters

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties of the Ti-Ni high-entropy alloy with and without thermomechanical treatment under elevated-temperature and extreme-environment testing conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermomechanical treatment does not improve the mechanical properties of the Ti-Ni high-entropy alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

AbstractCo-free body-centered cubic (bcc) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are prepared, and the elevated mechanical property and corrosion property of the Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mox (x = 0 and 0.1) alloys are studied. The Vickers hardness (HV) of the as-homogenized state is between HV 350 and HV 400. Both alloys are provided with nano-scale NiAl-rich B2 precipitates which contribute to the strength at high-temperature. In addition, adding Mo in the present alloy strengthens by σ phase. Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mo0.1 exhibited outstanding tensile properties, with a yield strength of 413 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 430 MPa in the elevated tensile test at 600 °C, which is better than that of Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5 alloy. Through potentiodynamic polarization testing in 0.5 M H2SO4 solution and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), it is shown that adding Mo can effectively reduce the corrosion current density and improve the impedance of passive film, since the passivation layer is formed and stable.Keywords: high-entropy alloys, body centered cubic, NiAl precipitates, high-temperature tensile, corrosion, EIS

Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility). In addition, hot rolling effectively eliminated the defects of the MEAs; under a given yield strength, hot-rolled MEAs exhibited superior ductility relative to non-hot-rolled MEAs. Studies of lightweight Ti-rich MEAs [] have explored finetuned Ti65(AlCrNbV)35 alloy compositions and have added various amounts of atomic radius zirconium (Zr) to enhance the mechanical properties of these MEAs through substitutional solid solution strengthening. To further improve the mechanical properties of these MEAs, two thermomechanical processing routes have been tested; the first is cold rolling 70% (CR70) followed by rapid annealing, and the second is hot rolling 50% plus cold rolling 70% (HR50CR70) followed by rapid annealing. In addition, the relationship between the rapid annealing temperature and the microstructure and mechanical properties of MEAs was investigated.

decision.rationale: Direction A is chosen because it directly addresses the question by proposing a thermomechanical treatment to improve the mechanical properties of the Ti-Ni high-entropy alloy. The critic's review suggests that this direction is viable with changes, and the fix is to investigate the robustness of the thermomechanical treatment parameters to ensure reproducibility and scalability. This direction has supporting evidence from the eligible evidence records, such as PMC9506522 and PMC8836748, which demonstrate the effectiveness of thermomechanical treatment in improving the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
